reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the still-open wound, a plausible first repair step.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound and prepare it for repair.

alternatives.reason: The signals may also initiate a blood supply for the repair.

effect: Debris has been cleared, and the wound now has explicit supply, surface and support slots to fill.
reaction: The slots make the remaining repair tasks clearer.
reason: The repair signals point toward the nearby vessel, suggesting a way to develop the wound's supply.
expectation: The signals will stimulate a vessel response that helps supply the wound.

effect: The signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, which looks suitable for the supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the parent vessel makes its role clear.
reason: The new vessel branch appears to provide the wound's missing supply.
expectation: The sprout will fill the supply slot and bring blood closer to the wound.

effect: The sprout filled the supply slot and formed a connected blood-flow route to the wound.
reaction: The completed vessel loop makes the supply role concrete.
reason: The fibroblast picture shows a collagen gene, and the RNA building blocks are headed to the same cell's nucleus, suggesting the first step toward making support.
expectation: The fibroblasts will make an RNA message for collagen production.

effect: The fibroblasts now have collagen messenger RNA, ready to guide protein production.
reaction: The DNA-to-RNA step makes the repair process clear.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids, which the fibroblasts can use to make collagen from the message.
expectation: The fibroblasts will produce collagen for wound support.

effect: Fibroblasts used the nutrients to make and export collagen, producing connective tissue for wound support.
reaction: The sequence connects the RNA message to repair material clearly.
reason: The new connective tissue appears suited to the wound's support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot in the healing wound.

effect: The new connective tissue filled the support slot, though the young tissue remains weaker than uninjured skin.
reaction: The strength limitation is a useful reminder that repair is not immediate restoration.
reason: Epidermal edge cells need nutrients to grow and close the remaining surface gap.
expectation: The cells will form a new surface layer for the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new epidermal sheet, ready to close the surface slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the closure easy to follow.
reason: The new surface fits the remaining surface slot in the healing wound.

choice.combine: Body with healing skin[Capillary sprout,New connective tissue]

expectation: The new epidermal sheet will close the wound surface.

effect: The new epidermal sheet closed the surface gap, completing the wound closure, support and supply goal; the deeper tissue is still strengthening.
reaction: The distinction between closure and full strength is useful.
reason: The remaining goal is to clear the temporary clot, and the enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin.

choice.combine: Body with healing skin[Capillary sprout,New connective tissue,New surface]

expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary fibrin clot while the repaired tissue remains.

effect: Clot-clearing enzymes removed most of the temporary fibrin, leaving closed skin and a scar that is still maturing; both goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between clearing the clot and continuing scar maturation is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen through an RNA message and amino acids was the most worthwhile passage: it connected familiar gene expression to a concrete repair material.

leastWorthwhile.text: Slotting the new surface into the wound was clear but predictable after the epidermal sheet had already formed.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a flow route, rather than simply ending at the wound; the young support tissue also remained weaker than uninjured skin.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; the named slots and picture descriptions made the choices understandable, although the sequence made overlapping repair jobs look more separate than the introduction suggests.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the repair sequence linked cell biology to a visible physiological outcome, while acknowledging that closure is not full recovery.
